Except that he isn't overpriced, as he is a 5 cap with 6 points in
disciplines. And 5 caps only get 5 points in abilities. So he is
getting THA instead of tha, but with a disadvantage to balance it out.

of him.

Action alone doesn't matter... it's "Action card". A vampire can hunt
with the default action as often as they like in a minion phase... but
they can't use a specific hunt action card more than once.

play (in this case it is the minon's own card text). That's what
limits it to once a minion phase.

"that turn" not "immediately")... the sequencing rule tells us exactly
how to deal with that.

To me, the fact that it doesn't say "at the end of the turn" means you
can do it at any point of the turn, provided the condition has been
met. Contrast this to Madness Network, which specifically states that
the acting methuselah must be finished with their minion actions
before you can start taking actions. Also, consider most cards the
impart abilities to other minions that don't necessarily have to be
done immediately after the play of that card. For example, Frontal
Assault giving minions a rush. They don't have to rush, and you're
free to do other actions beforehand. The card merely gives you the
ability within a certain window, in this case, during your minion
phase. For The Ankou, it's 'that turn when a vampire successfully
hunts'.

> > Hmm, still not sure. I would think that if titles are covered, that
> > they would have been specified, just as Clan and Sect were. I think
> > the fact that they are termed "titles" removes them from also being
> > traits, even though a title is a defining characteristic. Also, if
> > titles were considered traits for this card, could we not then use
> > more specific titles? Play one Second Tradition as the Prince of New
> > York, then a second as Prince of London, etc.
>
> Well, like I said, I'm not certain on this.  You may be right.  I
> don't think there's a strict definition of "trait", and so I think
> title might qualify.  On the other hand, it does open up a lot of
> questions on what counts as the same requirement that he can only meet
> once.

Likewise, I'm not sure either. It just seems to me that a title is
more a thing a vampire has, like a piece of equipment or a retainer. I
have a feeling that this question was missed during development of the
card. It would be nice to have a definition of traits in the new
rulebook, but I'm doubting this will be the case.

> > I would disagree on Flight being a trait. While it's not a discipline,
> > true, it also isn't a defining characteristic. You can say "Jack Drake
> > is an Anarch (vampire)", you couldn't say "Fidus is a Flight
> > (vampire)". You can say "Fidus has Flight, which allows him to use
> > these flight cards", much like you can say "Fidus has Fortitude, which
> > allows him to use these fortitude cards".
>
> Searching Google Group for flight+trait yields several results.  Most
> of them say that Flight *is* a trait, and one from LSJ implies
> otherwise, but doesn't, IMO, necessarily say that it is not.  I'm not
> sure what it *is* if not a trait.

The problem is, is that "Trait" is not a VTES word. There is nothing
in the rulebook pertaining to them, and no other card has referred to
'trait'. It's come into common usage as a way to describe attributes
like Sterile, Black Hand, etc. This has led me to consider that a
trait is a bolded term used or given to minions. And while a title is
also bolded, it is something more than a general trait, it's a Title,
much like Clan and Sect, while also bolded text, are more than just a
general trait and thus were specifically called out.

And while Flight isn't a discipline, it's for all intensive purposes
treated like one. So I would be inclined to lump it in with
Disciplines and Imbued Virtues, which I think parallel's LSJ's
thoughts when discussing Flight in regards to Seed of Corruption.

Leather Jacket can prevent outside combat, but only damage from an
opposing minion's strike. So, it can prevent the damage from Catatonic
Fear, but not from Horseshoes.

Blood Tears specifies that it can only prevent damage in combat.
